title: P3-E independent foundational-requirement reference record
description: One JSON object per line of bench/foundational_requirement_reference_v1.jsonl. Each line is ONE candidate 'foundational requirement' for one governed tool (or tool family), independently classified against a reproducible boundary test, with — where the frozen P3-B issue_refund corpus can exercise it — a per-case expected requirement-state / evidence-state table. This file is a REFERENCE authored from policy prose, tool argument schema, docs/threat-model.md, docs/gold-set-annotation.md and bench/label.py (an independent re-derivation of the refund rules). It is NOT derived from ControlPlane extraction output, the P1 verification ledger, any receipt, decide() output, cached _ClaimedFields, or existing verification coverage. It is FROZEN by sha256 before any measurement (see the .meta.json).

tool.description: a specific governed tool, or '<family>' when the requirement is family-wide

requirement_class.description: the P3-E classification, decided by the boundary_test below — NOT by the requirement's name and NOT by whether P3-A/P3-B previously filed it under foundational_requirements[]

required.description: a correct verifier of this tool must account for this condition

load_bearing.description: the action's safety materially depends on this condition; null when not applicable (e.g. a pure structural-validity check)

boundary_test.description: task P3-E section 12 — the formal claim vs precondition vs action-validity boundary test. Each answer is a fact about how the condition is (or would be) evaluated, cited in evidence_basis.

downstream_claims_gated.description: ClaimKind names whose verification becomes impossible/meaningless if this requirement is not met. Empty for ORDINARY_CLAIM / ACTION_VALIDITY_CHECK. Counted ONCE per requirement, never once per downstream claim.

expected_requirement_state_rule.description: the reproducible rule mapping observable facts -> {SATISFIED, VIOLATED, NOT_ESTABLISHED, NOT_APPLICABLE}

expected_evidence_state_rule.description: the reproducible rule mapping observable facts -> {AVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE, CONTRADICTORY, NOT_REQUIRED}

authoritative_basis.description: where the REQUIREMENT comes from: policy prose, a threat-model threat id, an action-semantics statement, a tool-arg-schema field, or a repo doc. Never a manifest claim_binding, never controlplane/ code behaviour.

evidence_basis.description: where the per-case STATE is read from: a human_label_sample.csv column, a gold_set.jsonl tool-call arg, a data/orders.db fixture cross-check, or bench/label.py. Never the P1 ledger / receipt / decide() output.

determinability.description: DETERMINABLE: an independent observer can fix the per-case state from the cited evidence, and the state varies with something other than one corpus construction parameter. DETERMINABLE_BUT_DEGENERATE: the per-case state is fixable but is a 1:1 recode of a single corpus construction parameter (task section 21 — denominator/identity concern). NOT_ASSESSABLE: no evidence channel exists in the integration as built (task section 16 — conceptually representable != runtime assessable).

per_case.description: present only for requirements the frozen 30-case P3-B issue_refund corpus can exercise. One entry per case_id in bench/human_label_sample.csv.

alt_reading.description: a defensible alternative state a different independent annotator would assign, when one exists — task section 21 test D (status corruption / judgement sensitivity)
